subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - Acme Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Anu Sharma <anu@acmehealth.com>, Tom Bennett <tom@acmehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - Acme Health

Hi Anu/Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps.

Key pain points (as I heard):
- Recent incidents: multiple latency spikes during high traffic windows (notably 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-07) causing timeouts for critical patient-facing flows.
- No consistent cross-region failover; current setup is single-region (us-west-2).
- Lack of transparent SLO tracking and alerts tied to business metrics.

Current stack you described:
- Model hosting on AWS EKS + SageMaker endpoints
- Custom routing layer in front of endpoints
- Internal caching layer but limited prefix/KV cache for chat histories

Success criteria you mentioned:
- 99.9% availability for inference APIs (business hours)
- p95 latency under 150ms for standard prompts
- Clear fallback behavior during model or region failures (graceful degradation)

How Redwood can help (high level):
- Multi-region routing + warm standby in secondary region
- Fallback model variants (smaller quantized model) to preserve availability under load
- Prefix/KV caching and batching to reduce p95 latency and cost
- SLO/SLA proposal and observability to tie alerts to user impact

Next steps:
1) Technical deep dive with your infra owners (we suggest 60m) — propose Wed 11/11 or Thu 11/12, 10am PT.
2) Send over incident logs (short export) and any runbooks you have — will help scope canary/failover tests.
3) Security/compliance contact — we can run through the questionnaire once we have your point of contact.

I've attached the quick meeting notes from today (discovery-notes.pdf).

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - Acme Health

Ben,

Thanks for the concise recap — this matches our notes.
Couple clarifications:
- Incident history: the Sept 21 event was a downstream DB throttling that amplified latency; Oct 7 was an autoscaling delay that led to 504s for ~18 minutes.
- Our primary concern is patient-facing latency — when requests timeout we lose session state and have to rebuild context which is the real user-visible failure.
- We currently have no automated cross-region failover; the DR plan is manual.

We can share the CloudWatch/Datadog timelines and the runbook snippets — I'll loop in our infra lead (Tom) and security (cc'd).

Tom, are you available Wed 11/11 10am PT for the deep dive?

-Anu

Ben/Team,

Great notes — some tactical items we should bring to the deep dive:
- Proposed canary plan: 5% traffic to a dedicated Redwood model variant in us-west-2 for 48h, with auto-fallback to a quantized gpt-small variant on threshold breach.
- Cross-region strategy: warm standby in us-east-1 with automated routing using latency + availability policy; idea is <60s RTO for routing changes.
- Observability: we can provide per-route p95/p99 dashboards, token-level cost and an \"impact score\" mapping timeouts to user sessions.
- SLAs: we can commit to 99.9% availability on Dedicated contracts; for Hosted API we'll propose an SLA + credits for reproducible outages.

I'll bring the SLA brief and a sample runbook for the canary. Ben, can you confirm the deep-dive time and invite our infra engineer (Jonas will pair if needed)?

-Marissa
